nodes.title: Troubleshooting methodology: Key Ideas
nodes.content: A structured troubleshooting process beats random guessing every time. The classic flow: identify the problem precisely, form a theory, test it, fix, verify, document. Most exams test that you know the flow AND can spot the layer at which the symptom originates.

flashcards.back: CompTIA's 6-step: (1) Identify the problem (gather symptoms, questions to user, recent changes). (2) Establish a theory of probable cause. (3) Test the theory. (4) Plan and implement the fix. (5) Verify full system functionality, apply preventive measures. (6) Document everything.

flashcards.front: Top-down vs bottom-up troubleshooting on a network problem.
flashcards.back: Top-down: start at the application layer and work down — does the browser work? DNS? TCP? Routing? Bottom-up: start at the physical layer — is the cable plugged in? Link light? IP? When you suspect physical/cable, bottom-up is faster. When the user has 'a website is broken', top-down is faster.

Almost every production incident traces back to a recent change — a deploy, a config push, a vendor patch, a cert rotation. 'It was working yesterday' tells you to check today's change-log before forming an exotic theory. Recent changes are the highest-priors of the bug space.

Bisect the path between symptom and cause. If 10 hops between client and server, test hop 5. Good → problem is past hop 5. Bad → problem is before. Two more bisections narrow it to one hop. Faster than checking every link sequentially when the chain is long.

pairs.stem: A sysadmin wants a new systemd service called 'appd' to start automatically at multi-user.target. Which directive in the [Install] section of the unit file is required?
A Linux administrator needs to add a kernel module for a new network card without rebooting the system. The module is called 'e1000e'. Which command accomplishes this?
A user account 'jsmith' needs to be locked immediately without deleting the account or its data. Which command achieves this?

A process is consuming excessive CPU. Running 'ps aux' shows PID 4521 using 98% CPU. The administrator wants to terminate it gracefully first, then forcefully if needed. In what order should signals be sent?
pairs.option: SIGKILL (9), then SIGTERM (15) if it persists

pairs.stem: After running 'useradd -m -s /bin/bash -G wheel devuser', the administrator checks /etc/passwd and sees devuser's primary group is 'devuser', not 'wheel'. Why?
pairs.option: The -G flag sets the primary group, which was overridden by useradd defaults

pairs.stem: An administrator needs to create a 10 GB logical volume named 'datalv' in a volume group named 'datavg'. Which command is correct?

nodes.title: Security fundamentals: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Security is about layering defenses so no single failure compromises a system. Most exams test the same core ideas: least privilege, defense in depth, the CIA triad, and the shared-responsibility line between you and your cloud provider.

flashcards.back: Confidentiality (only the right people see the data), Integrity (data isn't tampered with), Availability (the system is reachable when needed). Every security control maps to at least one of these three pillars.
Grant each identity (user, role, service account) the minimum permissions needed to do its job — no more. The opposite is wildcard access, which makes a single credential leak catastrophic.
Stack multiple, independent controls so an attacker has to defeat all of them. Example: WAF in front of an app, network ACL on the subnet, IAM on the workload, encryption at rest in the database.

flashcards.front: Shared responsibility model — who does what?
flashcards.back: The cloud provider secures the cloud (physical hardware, hypervisor, region facilities). You secure what's IN the cloud (your data, IAM config, OS patching on EC2, application code). The exact line shifts by service: serverless is more on the provider, IaaS is more on you.

pairs.stem: A security audit reveals that /etc/passwd is world-writable. Which command fixes this to the correct permissions (readable by all, writable only by root)?
A server running RHEL shows the following in 'journalctl -xe': 'kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 3201 (java) score 890'. What is the correct interpretation?
pairs.option: A cgroup memory limit was reached and the kernel killed the process to enforce the limit

pairs.stem: An administrator wants to prevent a specific kernel module 'pcspkr' from loading at boot. Which method is correct?
An administrator needs to set a file permission of rwxr-x--- (owner: rwx, group: r-x, other: none) using chmod with numeric notation. Which command is correct?

After rebooting a system, an administrator notices that a custom service file at /etc/systemd/system/myapp.service has been changed on disk but systemd is still using the old version. What must the administrator run?
A Bash script exits with code 127. What does this exit code specifically indicate?
pairs.option: The script ran successfully but returned an error from an internal function

pairs.stem: A cron job must run a backup script every day at 2:30 AM. Which crontab entry is correct?
A Bash script must check if a file exists before processing it. Which conditional expression is correct?
An administrator needs to replace every occurrence of 'localhost' with '127.0.0.1' in /etc/myapp.conf in place. Which sed command is correct?
An administrator needs to extract only the third field (colon-delimited) from /etc/passwd to list all usernames. Which command is correct?
A team wants to create a feature branch named 'feature/auth' from main and switch to it in one command. Which git command achieves this?
A script needs to count how many times the word 'ERROR' appears in /var/log/app.log. Which command produces only the count?
pairs.option: All of the above produce the same output

pairs.stem: A systemd service 'webapp' keeps failing. Running 'systemctl status webapp' shows 'Active: failed (Result: exit-code)'. Which command shows the detailed failure reason from the service's log output?
A script is failing intermittently in production. To debug it, an administrator wants to trace every command executed and its expanded value. Which bash invocation enables this tracing?

A user reports they cannot log in with their password. The administrator checks /etc/shadow and sees the account entry as: 'alice:!$6$hash...:19000:0:90:7:::'. What does the '!' prefix on the password hash indicate?
pairs.option: The password field uses a different hashing algorithm than SHA-512

pairs.stem: A Linux server's /var partition is 100% full, causing application failures. The administrator identifies large rotated logs in /var/log. Which sequence of commands frees space and prevents recurrence?

An administrator uses 'ip route show' and sees 'default via 192.168.1.1 dev eth0'. When they try to reach an external server, connections time out. 'ping 192.168.1.1' succeeds. What should the administrator check next?
pairs.option: Check if the default gateway 192.168.1.1 has internet connectivity and if NAT or firewall rules are blocking outbound traffic

pairs.stem: An administrator needs to troubleshoot why a network service is not listening on port 8080. Which command shows all listening TCP sockets with the associated process name?
